title: Fix dispatch (bounce / advisory / conflict / stacked-rebase)
summary: A PR owed a fix (review:changes bounce, an advisory finding on a needs-human PR, a mechanical conflict-fix bounce, or a stacked-base rebase) is picked up by the fix-dispatch daemon's 120s tick, gated on the daemon's own clone being fresh and Claude login being healthy, claimed per (repo,PR,head-sha), and either resumed or freshly spawned as a Claude session. The spawned session starts in a scratch cwd that is NOT its lane; it only reaches its lane later, itself, mid-session, with no permission grant from the dispatcher — the #2701 gap. It exits by posting a marker comment and handing back to ordinary review/CI.

provides.name: git
provides.note: resolved off the plist PATH; not independently verified installed at that PATH

provides.name: gh
provides.note: same PATH; gh calls are pervasive through this flow

provides.name: github-app-token
provides.note: withGithubAppAuth wraps buildCliDaemonEffects; mints a token at runtime from the WE_GITHUB_APP_ID/INSTALLATION_ID env pair

provides.name: <state-root>
provides.note: resolveCoordinationRoot(), WE_COORDINATION_ROOT-overridable; fix-dispatch-claim.mjs pins claims under it

states.label: PR owed a fix (bounce / advisory / conflict / stacked-rebase)
states.notes: Five populations funnel here on every ~120s tick (DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS, skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:76): ordinary review:changes bounce (OWED.bounced='fix', reconcile-core.mjs:239, capped by NEGOTIATION_ROUND_CAP=5 at reconcile-core.mjs:1257-1263), advisory-fix on a needs-human PR (reconcile-core.mjs:990-1059, ADVISORY_FIX_ROUND_CAP=3 at :276), mechanical conflict-fix bounce (reconcile-core.mjs:1211-1234, CONFLICT_FIX_ROUND_CAP=3 at :264), and stacked-base mechanical rebase (reconcile-core.mjs:1062-1119, same conflict-fix cap). Red CI is dispatched by a DIFFERENT operation (ci-heal-pr-dispatch.mjs) under kind:'ci-heal', not part of this flow. A 'no free lane' refusal (reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:1016) just leaves the PR here for the next tick, at no cost.

states.label: Daemon's own clone refused as stale

wait.for: the daemon's own managed clone to resync onto origin/main

states.notes: assertMainNotStale (called from scripts/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:939,1093) THROWS with STALE_MAIN_REFUSAL_MARKER (scripts/lib/main-staleness.mjs:140) for a diverged/dirty/off-base/behind managed clone rather than dispatch on possibly-stale code. withSelfSync's hasStaleRefusal hook (wired at skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:678-680, matched via hasStaleMainRefusal at :336) triggers an immediate rebuild (scripts/lib/daemon-self-sync.mjs:594-595); on success onRestart calls process.exit(0) (skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:672-675) and launchd KeepAlive (launchd:com.we.fix-dispatch-daemon.plist, KeepAlive=true) relaunches it onto the fresh clone. A rebuild that keeps failing just logs 'retrying next tick' (scripts/lib/daemon-self-sync.mjs:525-531) with NO cap on how many ticks this can repeat and no escalation to a human if the clone stays stale indefinitely.

states.label: Claude login broken — fix dispatch paused for the tick

wait.for: `claude auth status --json` to report logged-in again

states.notes: Computed once per daemon tick (skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:477) from readClaudeAuthHealth (scripts/conveyor/claude-auth-health.mjs:134) OR'd with a cheap probeClaudeLoggedIn (:156). While paused, fix AND ci-heal are both skipped outright with no round-cap comment spent (skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:488-491). Self-clears purely via next tick's cheap probe; nothing pages a human beyond the daemon's own stderr log line (AUTH_PAUSE_LOG_MESSAGE, scripts/conveyor/claude-auth-health.mjs:67).

states.label: Heavy-test queue projected wait exceeds budget

retries.what: durable queue-cap refusals, counted by QUEUE_CAP_REFUSAL_MARKER comments on the PR itself (restart-surviving, scripts/conveyor/queue-cap-refusal-count.mjs)

states.notes: #4229 (bornAs 4229, epic #4075/#3383) — FIXED. createQueueBudget (scripts/readiness/heavy-queue-projection.mjs:271, imported reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:79) still refuses 'queue-cap' every pass while the projected heavy-slot demand exceeds budget — dispatch keeps retrying, exactly as before, since queue congestion is expected to clear on its own (queue-cap-refusal-count.mjs's own header). What changed: each of the first 3 refusals now posts a durable, PR-comment-backed marker (recordQueueCapRefusal, reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:1161), so a restart never resets the count.

states.label: Durable queue-cap refusal cap reached (3) — surfaced, monitoring continues

escalation.how: round-cap-exhausted note (capKind: 'queue-cap') → PR comment (scripts/conveyor/reconcile-note-comment.mjs#postNoteComment, reused verbatim) + desktop notify (scripts/conveyor/branch-sync.mjs#notifyDesktopChecked)

states.notes: #4229 — STILL REFUSES, never gives up: dispatch keeps recomputing tryAdmit every pass exactly as before (queue-cap-hit's own transition back to pr-flagged-for-fix is unchanged) — this state is the one-time note event, then ordinary retrying resumes. The note's episode key is the (attempts, cap) pair (round-cap-exhausted's own dedup, reconcile-note-comment.mjs#noteEpisodeKey), so the SAME exhaustion posts exactly once; a human letting it retry past a reset and burning through the cap again is a genuinely new episode.

states.label: Resume-or-nothing attempted for a conflict-caused entry

wait.for: a `claude agents --json --all` listing to confirm the resumed session took

states.notes: Only eligible for a conflict-caused bounce (entry.isConflict); every other kind returns resumed:false at no lane/claim cost (reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:474-524 docblock). Internally acquires its own (repo,pr,headSha) claim via acquireFixDispatchClaim (same TTL=10m / no-PID-fast-reclaim caveats as the claim step under fixer-spawned, scripts/conveyor/fix-dispatch-claim.mjs:56). Isolated in its own try/catch (reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:999-1006) so its own documented flakiness (a real listing race, #3331) never aborts the whole tick's other dispatches.

states.label: Fixer Claude session spawned (fresh dispatch or confirmed resume)
states.notes: See this state's own steps for the #2701 permission-prompt bug: the session's real cwd (a scratch dir) and the lane it must later edit are two different places, and nothing in the dispatch path grants edit permission on the lane before or during spawn.

states.label: Fixer blocked on an unanswered Claude Code permission prompt
states.owner: scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs#isAwaitingPermission / assessLiveness (detects and refuses re-dispatch; does not resolve it)

wait.for: a human to answer the pending Claude Code permission prompt

escalation.how: a surfaced note + PR comment naming the stuck cwd, waitingFor reason, and held-hours

states.notes: isAwaitingPermission (reconcile-core.mjs:444-447) flags agent.status==='waiting' with waitingFor matching /permission/i; assessLiveness ranks it FIRST (reconcile-core.mjs:706-713) so a fresh dispatch is refused while detected, and planReconcile surfaces a note + PR comment with held-hours (reconcile-core.mjs:857-868) — the code's own comment there says 'Three sessions have held one for 211.4 hours; a refusal buried in a list is how that stayed invisible.' But NOTHING kills, restarts, times out, or auto-clears the stuck process itself (zero waitingFor-specific handling in scripts/conveyor/session-reaper.mjs, confirmed by grep). Detection itself can SILENTLY LAPSE: the generic hung-transcript detector gives a pending-tool-use session a 3x grace (PENDING_CALL_GRACE_MULTIPLIER, scripts/conveyor/hung-session.mjs:79) over the 30-minute base threshold (:69) before marking it hung:true; once hung, assessLiveness's isFinished() filters it out BEFORE the awaiting-permission check is ever reached (reconcile-core.mjs:690-696) — so a permission-block surviving past ~90 minutes stops being surfaced at all and instead reads as 'nothing live', letting the reconciler dispatch a FRESH fixer into the same lane while the original session is still sitting there blocked. This is the #2701 shape precisely (a fixer sat 36 minutes on a prompt — still well inside the ~90-minute grace, so it WOULD have been surfaced, but nothing bounds even a correctly-surfaced block). The only actual remedy is a human running scripts/operations/clear-stuck-session.mjs by hand (documented at reconcile-core.mjs:174-178 as the intended, non-automatic path).

states.label: Fixer self-reported blocked-on-infra (rate limit / outage)

wait.for: INFRA_RETRY_COOLOFF_MS to elapse since the completion record's updatedAt

retries.what: blocked-on-infra self-report / cooloff / redispatch cycle, counted as a durable per-SESSION streak (`infraStreak`) the completion STORE's own write path maintains

states.notes: 4227 (epic #4075/#3383) — FIXED. session-reaper.mjs's completion resolver stops the OS process immediately once the record says done, regardless of outcome (reconcile-core.mjs:504-508 docblock) — only the RECORD's cool-off (awaitingInfraCooloff:true) keeps the PR from being redispatched during the 15-minute window (reconcile-core.mjs:553-584). The completion STORE's write path (scripts/operations/completion-store.mjs#writeCompletion) now persists a durable per-SESSION `infraStreak`/`infraStreakSince` across dispatch generations; at INFRA_RETRY_CAP (4) the cycle moves to `infra-retry-escalated` — the cool-off grows and a person is notified, without ever stopping the retry outright.

states.label: blocked-on-infra streak capped — escalated, cool-off lengthened

wait.for: the LENGTHENED 60-minute capped infra cool-off (INFRA_RETRY_CAPPED_COOLOFF_MS) before retrying again

states.notes: 4227 (epic #4075/#3383) — the retry is NEVER stopped outright (infra may still recover); it is only slowed and surfaced. The note's episode key is `kind + prNumber + since` (the streak's own first timestamp), so a streak that keeps growing past the cap posts as ONE episode, not a fresh comment every tick.

states.label: Fixer stood down — human judgment needed

escalation.how: durable PR comment (STAND_DOWN_MARKER); cleared or taken over via /finish

states.notes: Posted when the fixer can't safely judge (ambiguous finding, unresolved gate-red, a real conflict) — STAND_DOWN_MARKER (scripts/conveyor/stand-down.mjs:48). Terminal for the reconciler with no decay: countUnresolvedStandDowns (reconcile-core.mjs:472-485) is checked FIRST in planReconcile (reconcile-core.mjs:822-847), so this PR is refused every subsequent tick until a human clears it. 'The intended exit is a HUMAN — who reads the escalation, makes the judgment, and clears the marker (or takes the PR over via /finish)' (scripts/conveyor/stand-down.mjs:17-19). The comment is durable and visible on the PR but nothing proactively pages/notifies anyone — a human must be reading the PR thread.

states.label: Fixer posted its mode's marker comment and exited
states.notes: Exactly one of three markers gets posted depending on mode: ordinary bounce runs rearm-review.mjs, swapping review:changes->review:pending + REARM_COMMENT_MARKER (scripts/conveyor/rearm-review.mjs:40,73-78); advisory-fix mode posts ADVISORY_FIX_COMMENT_MARKER with NO label swap (scripts/conveyor/advisory-fix-mark.mjs:48,77-87); conflict-fix/stacked-rebase mode posts CONFLICT_FIX_COMMENT_MARKER via conflict-fix-mark.mjs, also no label touched (scripts/conveyor/conflict-fix-mark.mjs:45-58). The fixer then EXITS without merging, without releasing the lane, without touching CI directly (skills-src/conveyor/fix-agent-brief.md:427-439) — its process exit IS the completion signal.

states.label: Handed back to ordinary review / CI
states.notes: No wait/timeout is enforced by this flow's own code on the recheck step: runReconcileFixDispatch ends with a plain return and no polling loop after dispatch (scripts/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch.mjs:1020-1037). It is bounded only by the ordinary ~120s daemon tick cadence re-reading PR state fresh (DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS, skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:76) and by the SEPARATE review-dispatch daemon picking up the now-review:pending (or still-needs-human) PR — out of this flow's own file set.

states.label: Fix population's round cap reached
states.notes: 4227 (epic #4075/#3383) — FIXED. refuse('cap-exhausted', ...) fires for whichever population is stuck: ordinary bounce (reconcile-core.mjs:1422-1426, NEGOTIATION_ROUND_CAP=5), advisory-fix (reconcile-core.mjs:1171-1176, ADVISORY_FIX_ROUND_CAP=3), conflict-fix bounce (reconcile-core.mjs:1379-1384, CONFLICT_FIX_ROUND_CAP=3), or stacked-rebase (reconcile-core.mjs:1267-1272, same cap, capKind `stacked-rebase`). Every ONE of these now ALSO pushes a `kind:'round-cap-exhausted'` note (reconcile-core.mjs#refuseCapExhausted, :895-903) — the SAME 'refuse AND surface' shape the sibling ci-heal-exhausted path (reconcile-core.mjs:1103-1122) already used, now shared by every non-ci-heal cap population, each carrying `capKind` so the note names which population is exhausted (`fix`/`review`/`advisory-fix`/`conflict-fix`/`stacked-rebase`). Formerly a refusal-only entry (logged by the daemon's own formatRefusalLine, skills-src/conveyor/reconcile-fix-dispatch-daemon.mjs:520-538, to its own stderr/log file) — now also a durable PR comment via reconcile-note-comment.mjs and listed by `scripts/operations/operator-queue.mjs --with-reconcile-notes`.

states.label: Fixer self-reported blocked-on-permission

escalation.how: permission-blocked note → PR comment naming the denied command

states.notes: PR #3964: a permission wall requires a sanctioned helper or allow rule. Surface immediately; retry slowly without incrementing the infra streak.

transitions.on: daemon's own clone is behind/diverged from origin/main
Claude login broken this tick
the PR's own durable attempt count is at/above its population's cap
heavy-test queue projected wait exceeds budget
entry.isConflict — try a resume before ever popping a lane
non-conflict entry, or resume not attempted — pop a free lane and dispatch fresh
clone rebuilt/resynced and the daemon restarts onto new code (launchd KeepAlive relaunches it)
next tick's cheap claude auth status probe reports logged-in
next pass recomputes the queue budget fresh (below the durable cap — one more attempt marker posted)
the durable queue-cap-refusal count reaches its cap (3)
note posted (or already posted this episode); ordinary retrying resumes (still refuses, never given up on)
resume confirmed live
resume not confirmed after 3 listing re-reads — falls through to a fresh dispatch
claim held elsewhere / resume spawn threw
claim held elsewhere, or cwd-resolve/spawn threw — claim released, retried next tick
fixer's Bash/Edit inside its own lane is denied by Claude Code's own permission classifier, with nobody watching this session to answer it
fixer self-reports blocked-on-infra instead of finishing
fixer posts STAND_DOWN_MARKER
fixer completes: posts its marker and exits
~90 minutes pass and the hung-transcript detector silently reclassifies the session as not-live, even though it may still be sitting on the prompt (a double-dispatch risk, not a real fix)
a human manually answers the prompt, or runs clear-stuck-session.mjs and the session resumes and finishes
15-minute cooloff elapses (streak below INFRA_RETRY_CAP)
the durable per-session blocked-on-infra streak reaches INFRA_RETRY_CAP (4)
60-minute capped cooloff elapses
session exits
PR re-enters ordinary review/CI
fixer self-reports blocked-on-permission
60-minute permission cooloff elapses

steps.does: spawns `claude --resume` in the same per-session scratch cwd pattern as a fresh dispatch
claims (repo,pr,headSha) BEFORE building anything; on 'held' returns without spawning and the lane is returned to the pool
resolves the session's cwd to a per-session SCRATCH directory (.operations/dispatch/<sessionId>), a sibling of .lanes/ — never the lane clone, never the daemon's own checkout

writes a workspace-TRUST entry into ~/.claude.json for the scratch cwd only, so `claude --bg` doesn't refuse 'Workspace not trusted' — a trust entry, NOT a Claude settings permission rule, and scoped to the scratch dir only

provides.name: bash:<scratch>
provides.note: workspace trust only, scoped to <scratch>; NOT edit:<lane> or bash:<lane>

steps.does: spawns `claude --bg` with --settings carrying ONLY an env key (gh-shim PATH override + bash timeouts) — no --add-dir, no permission-mode flag, no settings.local write scoped to the lane; the code's own docblock says this is deliberate ('a dispatcher that hard-coded --dangerously-skip-permissions would silently widen...')

steps.actor: the fixer session itself, inside its own Bash tool (NOT the dispatcher)
steps.does: runs `lane-pool.mjs acquire ... && cd "$LANE"` per the brief's own step 1 — the ONLY place the fixer ever reaches its lane; the dispatcher never cd's it there and never scopes any permission to it first

assumes.name: edit:<lane>
assumes.note: ASSUMED by the brief's own step 1 (cd "$LANE" then edit) but never granted by anything upstream in this flow: lane-pool.mjs acquire writes no trust/settings.local entry for the lane (grep confirmed zero grantTrust/withTrustedDirs/settings.local hits in scripts/lane-pool.mjs), and the session's cwd at spawn time is the scratch dir, outside every constellation checkout's own .claude/settings.json ancestry. THIS IS THE #2701 GAP: nothing upstream of this step provides permission:edit:<lane>.
